A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Cameras as Relative Positional Encoding by the same authors. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on novel view synthesis, stereo depth estimation, spatial cognition, model scaling, and PRoPE component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds intrinsic-shift evaluations of LVSM and UniMatch in Appendix A.2.2.

M1.justification: PRoPE's projective transformations, RoPE components, GTA-style attention, and CamRay formulation are unchanged. The additional experiments evaluate existing encoding variants; the distorted-camera extension mentioned in the conclusion is future work.

E1.justification: The datasets and three principal tasks are retained. Appendix A.2.2 extends intrinsic-shift testing to stereo depth estimation and evaluates NVS zoom levels through 7×, beyond the original 5× range. These expand test scenarios without introducing a new application domain.

E2.justification: The depth comparison expands substantially: v1 Table 4 compares UniMatch with UniMatch+PRoPE, whereas v2 Table A.4 also evaluates Plücker, GTA, GTA+CamRay, and PRoPE+CamRay variants. Table A.3 additionally includes GTA+CamRay in intrinsic-shift NVS comparisons. These introduce meaningful camera-aware controls; the original comparator sets remain available.

E3.justification: The added studies use augmented intrinsics during training. Table A.3 specifies 1–3× training augmentation and tests 1×, 3×, 5×, and 7× zoom; Table A.4 tests 1×, 1.5×, 2×, and 3× with one-eighth of the original training resources. These are additional protocols, not documented revisions to the retained main experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.2.2 adds substantial controlled robustness analyses across LVSM and UniMatch, testing whether PRoPE's advantage persists when GTA receives intrinsics through CamRay and when test zoom changes. This extends v1's hybrid-encoding comparison and NVS robustness plots to a broader examination of intrinsic modeling. The original component ablation in Table A.1 is unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The percentage changes in Table A.4 report performance differences, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables A.3–A.4 add substantial zoom-dependent results. At 7× NVS zoom, PRoPE reports 22.40 PSNR versus GTA+CamRay's 21.77; at 3× depth zoom, their respective Abs Rel reductions against UniMatch are 26.40% and 13.65%. These are newly reported evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1. Existing main-table results, Table A.1, and the relocated CAT3D results are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, attention formulations, projective factorization, and invariance/reduction arguments are retained. Combining v1 Equations 4–5 into v2 Equation 4 and moving the properties into Section 3.5 changes presentation rather than mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions retain the same central claims: PRoPE encodes camera intrinsics and extrinsics relatively, improves multiview performance and generalization, and applies across tasks and model scales. The added experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly identifies distorted camera models as an extension requiring, for example, per-patch projective approximations. Appendix A.2.2 also interprets the added comparisons as further support for attention-level intrinsic conditioning when competing methods receive equivalent camera information. Existing numerical-stability and noncommutativity limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table A.4 newly specifies two GPUs and 50,000 training steps for the added depth study. Conversely, Section 4.1 removes v1's explanation that fixed embeddings pad inputs when raymaps are absent, while retaining the matched-model-size statement. Appendix A.1 and the code-access statement remain unchanged; the deleted explanation does not establish an implementation change.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yi et al., Estimating Body and Hand Motion in an Ego-Sensed World, to the related-work discussion of relative parameters and reference-frame dependence. The positioning relative to raymaps, CaPE, GTA, and RoPE otherwise remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 tightens prose, corrects several grammatical errors, removes the unfinished Section 3 introduction and the experiments roadmap, and shortens the conclusion. It gives PRoPE's properties a separate subsection and inserts Appendix A.2.2, renumbering the retained qualitative-depth subsection. The overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the multi-part Tables A.3–A.4, relocates CAT3D Table 7 to Table A.2, and compacts and regroups existing displays. The appendix qualitative figures are redistributed across pages. Existing diagrams, plots, and qualitative examples are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The added camera-aware depth controls and intrinsic-shift comparisons strengthen the evidence for PRoPE's encoding design, while editing improves clarity. The gain is tempered by incomplete identification of the new depth evaluation's dataset aggregation, unreconciled GTA SSIM/LPIPS entries at 1× in Table A.3 versus Tables 2–3, and removal of the fixed-padding implementation detail. The revision provides useful additional support without substantially changing the established contribution.
